profile.name: Reza Nasirian
profile.tagline: I build LLM agents that let people talk to their data — and the data platforms underneath them.
profile.about_text:
Most people who build AI systems have never had to answer for a wrong number in a board report. I have. I spent three years as a BI developer — modelling cubes, writing the queries behind dashboards, and learning exactly how messy real enterprise data is before it reaches a chart.

That is why I moved into AI engineering rather than starting there. When I build a multi-agent system that writes MDX against a production cube, I already know where the joins lie and which numbers users will not forgive being wrong. The retrieval problems I care about — a tax statute whose meaning depends on its position in a hierarchy — are structural problems, not embedding problems.

Right now I am working on fine-tuning and local model deployment, because the enterprises with the most interesting data are the ones that cannot send it to an external API.

projects.title: TaxSage — Graph-based RAG for Tax Law
projects.problem: Iranian tax law is a hierarchy: articles carry notes, notes carry amendments, and a clause often means nothing without its parent. Flat vector search returns passages that read similarly but sit in the wrong branch, so the chatbot cites the wrong rule.
projects.approach: Modelled the statute as a graph so retrieval follows the legal hierarchy before ranking, backed by a Qdrant vector store and orchestrated with LangChain. Served over FastAPI to taxpayers and the general public.

projects.title: CubeAgent — Conversational Multi-Agent BI
projects.problem: Business users needed answers from OLAP cubes but could not write MDX, so every question became a ticket for an analyst — and the analyst became the bottleneck.
projects.approach: Built a multi-agent framework where specialized agents split the work: one interprets the question, one generates and validates MDX against the cube schema, one chooses the visualization. Responses stream over Server-Sent Events, and the orchestration layer is modular so agents can be swapped without touching the core.

experience.title: AI Engineer — LLM Agents
experience.description:
• Built and shipped a multi-agent system that lets business users query OLAP cubes in plain language, with specialized agents for interpretation, MDX generation and visualization coordinated through LangChain.
• Designed a graph-based RAG system over Iranian tax law, modelling the statute hierarchy as a graph so retrieval follows legal structure rather than flat similarity.
• Implemented streaming responses over Server-Sent Events and a modular orchestration layer, so new agents can be added without changes to the core.
• Working on fine-tuning and local model deployment to remove the dependency on external APIs for privacy-sensitive data.

experience.title: Business Intelligence Developer
experience.description:
• Designed and shipped interactive dashboards in Dundas BI that the group used for day-to-day decision-making.
• Built an API generator that produces REST endpoints — including filter conditions — from arbitrary database tables without writing code.
• Modelled multi-dimensional OLAP cubes in SSAS and wrote the MDX and SQL behind the reporting layer.
• Extended dashboard behaviour with custom JavaScript beyond what the platform offered out of the box.
• Integrated third-party web services with Python to widen the range of reportable data sources.
